category: More phrasal verbs on irregular bases: M-Z

entries.meaning: To pretend that something is true, especially as a game. ---
examples: The kids make believe the couch is a pirate ship.
We made believe we hadn't seen him come in.
She spent the whole afternoon making believe she was a doctor.
entries.русский: притворяться, притвориться; играть в воображаемое; воображать
entries.separable: fixed — believe is part of the verb and never moves; what you pretend comes after as a clause: make believe you're asleep
entries.forms: make believe · made believe · made believe
entries.transitivity: intransitive — it takes a clause, not an object: made believe he hadn't heard

entries.meaning: To put money into a fund, a plan, or a shared pot. ---
examples: Everybody in the office pays in ten dollars a week.
He paid in for thirty years and drew his first check at sixty-five.
By then she had paid in more than the policy was ever going to return.
entries.русский: вносить, внести (деньги); отчислять, отчислить; делать взносы
entries.separable: separable, but it very often stands alone: you pay in for forty years. With an amount both orders work — pay in two hundred a month, pay it in
entries.forms: pay in · paid in · paid in
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (we both pay in every month), transitive (paid in another five hundred)

entries.meaning: To give someone official access to information they were not allowed to have before. ---
examples: Only four people have been read in on the project.
They read her in the day she transferred.
I'll read in the rest of the team on Monday.
entries.русский: посвящать, посвятить (в курс дела); допускать, допустить к закрытой информации
entries.separable: separable, and usually split — the person goes in the middle: read her in, read the new analyst in; what she is told follows on: read him in on the plan
entries.forms: read in · read in · read in

entries.meaning: To learn about a subject by reading as much as you can about it. ---
examples: Read up on the company before the interview.
I read up on Texas water law all weekend.
She's been reading up about adoption for months.
entries.русский: изучать, изучить (материал); читать, почитать о чём-л.; подчитывать
entries.separable: no object of its own — the subject follows on or about: read up on the case; never ✗ read the case up
entries.forms: read up · read up · read up
entries.transitivity: intransitive — always with on or about

entries.meaning: To go to someone for help or sympathy instead of handling something yourself. ---
examples: Don't run to me when the landlord calls.
He ran to his father the second things got hard.
She's run to the same friend with every problem since college.
entries.русский: бежать жаловаться (кому-л.); обращаться, обратиться за помощью
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows to: run to her lawyer, run to me; never ✗ run me to
entries.forms: run to · ran to · run to

entries.meaning: To reach a particular total or size. ---
examples: The repair bill ran to almost four thousand dollars.
His report runs to three hundred pages.
By the time we were finished, the list had run to sixty names.
entries.русский: составлять, составить (сумму); доходить до, достигать; насчитывать
entries.separable: inseparable — the amount follows to: ran to four thousand dollars; never ✗ ran the bill to
entries.forms: run to · ran to · run to

entries.meaning: To understand the hidden truth or the real nature of something. ---
examples: A good teacher can see into a kid's silence.
She saw into his motives long before the rest of us did.
Nobody has ever really seen into that family.
entries.русский: понимать скрытую суть; видеть насквозь; разбираться в чём-л.
entries.separable: inseparable — what you understand follows into: see into his motives, see into it; never ✗ see his motives into
entries.forms: see into · saw into · seen into

entries.meaning: To walk through a building or property and look at all of it. ---
examples: We drove out to see over the barn before making an offer.
They saw over three apartments in one afternoon.
The place had already been seen over by two other buyers.
entries.русский: осматривать, осмотреть (дом, помещение); обходить с осмотром
entries.separable: inseparable — the place follows over: see over the house, see over it. Americans more often say look over or walk through; see over has a slightly formal, real-estate ring to it
entries.forms: see over · saw over · seen over

entries.meaning: To close an opening or a tear with stitches. ---
examples: She sewed up the tear before anyone noticed.
The doctor had the cut sewn up in ten minutes.
Give me the jacket and I'll sew the pocket up.
entries.русский: зашивать, зашить; сшивать, сшить; заштопать
entries.separable: separable — sew up the hem, sew the hem up, sew it up; a pronoun has to sit in the middle, never ✗ sew up it
entries.forms: sew up · sewed up · sewn up

entries.meaning: To settle something completely so that the outcome is no longer in doubt. ---
examples: Two more states and she has the nomination sewn up.
They sewed up the contract over dinner.
Don't worry about the venue — I'll sew that up tomorrow.
entries.русский: обеспечивать, обеспечить (победу, сделку); улаживать, уладить окончательно
entries.separable: separable — sew up the deal, sew the deal up, sew it up; the passive it's all sewn up is the form you hear most
entries.forms: sew up · sewed up · sewn up

entries.meaning: To destroy something by shooting at it. ---
examples: Somebody shot out the streetlights on our block.
The deputy shot the tires out and the truck slid to a stop.
Two windows had been shot out during the night.
entries.русский: расстреливать, расстрелять (что-л.); выбивать, выбить выстрелом
entries.separable: separable — shoot out the tires, shoot the tires out, shoot them out; never ✗ shoot out them
entries.forms: shoot out · shot out · shot out

entries.meaning: To move out or forward suddenly and very fast. ---
examples: His hand shot out and caught the glass before it hit the floor.
Flames shoot out of that pipe every time they test the burner.
A cat came shooting out from under the porch.
entries.русский: вылетать, вылететь; выбрасываться, выброситься (резко); метнуться
entries.separable: no object — his hand shot out; the two words stay together
entries.forms: shoot out · shot out · shot out

entries.meaning: To settle a fight or a contest in one final exchange. ---
examples: The two of them shot it out on Main Street at noon.
The robbers had shot it out with police for twenty minutes before they surrendered.
If the game is still tied, they'll shoot it out from the penalty spot.
entries.русский: устраивать перестрелку; решать, решить исход в финальной серии
entries.separable: the object is fixed — always shoot it out, never ✗ shoot out it; the opponent follows with: shoot it out with the police
entries.forms: shoot out · shot out · shot out
entries.transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object it

entries.meaning: To pass through something suddenly and fast, especially a pain or a feeling. ---
examples: A sharp pain shot through my knee when I stood up.
Panic shoots through you the second the alarm goes off.
She could feel the cold shooting through her wet coat.
entries.русский: пронзать, пронзить; простреливать (о боли); проноситься, пронестись сквозь
entries.separable: inseparable — what it passes through follows through: shot through my knee, shot through her; never ✗ shot my knee through
entries.forms: shoot through · shot through · shot through

entries.meaning: To lower yourself into a seated position, or to put someone else into one. ---
examples: Please sit down — the movie is about to start.
We had barely sat down when the power went out.
She sat her son down and asked him what had happened.
entries.русский: садиться, сесть; усаживать, усадить
entries.separable: usually no object — sit down and eat. With an object it splits: sit the kids down, sat him down; never ✗ sit down him
entries.forms: sit down · sat down · sat down
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (please sit down), transitive (sat the kids down at the table)

entries.meaning: To meet with someone in order to talk something through seriously. ---
examples: The two sides finally sat down last Thursday.
We need to sit down with our accountant before April.
They've been sitting down with the union every week since March.
entries.русский: садиться за стол переговоров; встречаться, встретиться для обсуждения
entries.separable: no object — the other side follows with: sit down with the union; what you discuss follows and: sit down and work it out
entries.forms: sit down · sat down · sat down

entries.meaning: To move sideways along a seat or bench to make room for someone. ---
examples: Slide over — there's room for one more.
She slid over so he could get into the booth.
Everybody kept sliding over until the whole bench was full.
entries.русский: подвигаться, подвинуться (в сторону); отодвигаться, отодвинуться
entries.separable: no object — slide over and let me sit; nothing comes between the two words
entries.forms: slide over · slid over · slid over

entries.meaning: To push something across a flat surface toward someone. ---
examples: He slid the envelope over without saying a word.
Slide over the salt, would you?
I've slid the file over to your side of the desk.
entries.русский: придвигать, придвинуть; подвигать, подвинуть (по поверхности)
entries.separable: separable — slide over the check, slide the check over, slide it over; never ✗ slide over it
entries.forms: slide over · slid over · slid over

entries.meaning: To insist on something as a right, or to rest your case on it. ---
examples: He stood on his right to remain silent.
I'll stand on my record and let the voters decide.
We have never stood on ceremony in this house.
entries.русский: настаивать на (своих правах); держаться за; опираться на
entries.separable: inseparable — what you insist on follows on: stand on your rights, stand on it; never ✗ stand it on
entries.forms: stand on · stood on · stood on

entries.meaning: To stay right next to someone and watch them while they work. ---
examples: I can't cook with you standing over me.
The nurse stood over him until he swallowed the pill.
He has stood over every batch since the recall.
entries.русский: стоять над душой; надзирать, следить за работой; контролировать
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows over: stand over him, stand over the students; never ✗ stand him over
entries.forms: stand over · stood over · stood over

entries.meaning: To fasten something flat against a surface with glue or tape. ---
examples: Stick that corner down before somebody trips on it.
He stuck down the loose tile with a little glue.
The edges had been stuck down with masking tape.
entries.русский: приклеивать, приклеить; заклеивать, заклеить; прилеплять
entries.separable: separable — stick down the flap, stick the flap down, stick it down; never ✗ stick down it
entries.forms: stick down · stuck down · stuck down

entries.meaning: To draw a line through written words to cancel them. ---
examples: Strike through anything on the form that no longer applies.
She struck through the last two lines and initialed the change.
The old price had been struck through and a lower one written above it.
entries.русский: вычёркивать, вычеркнуть; зачёркивать, зачеркнуть
entries.separable: usually kept together — strike through the wrong answer; a pronoun can come between: strike it through. The passive is very common: the clause was struck through
entries.forms: strike through · struck through · struck through

entries.meaning: To obtain a legal document such as a warrant by making a sworn statement. ---
examples: She swore out a complaint against her landlord the next morning.
A warrant had already been sworn out for his arrest.
If he comes anywhere near the house, we'll swear out a restraining order.
entries.русский: получать, получить (ордер) по заявлению под присягой; подавать заявление под присягой
entries.separable: separable — swear out a warrant, swear a warrant out, swear it out; the object is the document, not the person, who follows against: swore out a complaint against him
entries.forms: swear out · swore out · sworn out

entries.meaning: To get rid of an illness or a substance by sweating. ---
examples: He's in the sauna trying to sweat out a cold.
She sweated out the fever under three blankets.
Whatever it was, he had sweated it out by Sunday.
entries.русский: выгонять, выгнать потом (простуду); пропотеть и выздороветь; выводить с потом
entries.separable: separable — sweat out a cold, sweat the cold out, sweat it out; never ✗ sweat out it
entries.forms: sweat out · sweated out · sweated out

entries.meaning: To wait anxiously through something you cannot control. ---
examples: We sweated out the last two minutes of the game.
She's still sweating out the results of the blood test.
There's nothing to do now but sweat it out.
entries.русский: томиться в ожидании; мучительно ждать; переживать до конца
entries.separable: separable — sweat out the verdict, sweat the verdict out, sweat it out; the form with the empty it is the commonest of all: we just had to sweat it out
entries.forms: sweat out · sweated out · sweated out

entries.meaning: To move or toss something violently in all directions. ---
examples: The storm threw the boat about for six hours.
Passengers were thrown about the cabin when the plane dropped.
Stop throwing your clothes about the room.
entries.русский: разбрасывать, разбросать; швырять из стороны в сторону; мотать (о качке)
entries.separable: separable — throw the papers about, throw them about, throw about the papers; the passive is where you hear it most: we were thrown about the cabin
entries.forms: throw about · threw about · thrown about

entries.meaning: To drink something quickly, in one swallow. ---
examples: He tossed off the whiskey and reached for his coat.
She tossed the last of the coffee off and headed for the door.
Two shots had been tossed off before the toast even finished.
entries.русский: выпивать залпом, выпить залпом; опрокидывать, опрокинуть (стакан)
entries.separable: separable — toss off a beer, toss the beer off, toss it off; never ✗ toss off it
entries.forms: toss off · tossed off · tossed off

entries.meaning: To produce something quickly and without much effort.
examples: He tossed off a two-page reply in about ten minutes.
She can toss off a watercolor between classes.
The song was tossed off in one afternoon and it sold a million copies.
entries.русский: делать, сделать наспех; выдавать, выдать на скорую руку; строчить
entries.separable: separable — toss off a reply, toss a reply off, toss it off; never ✗ toss off it
entries.forms: toss off · tossed off · tossed off
